result.topic_en: Evaluation of quadratic Gauss sums $\sum \cos(s^2 2\pi/n+\delta)$ by means of the Fresnel integral and Fourier series (Poisson summation), with the multiplicativity of $\varphi(m,n)=\sum e^{ms^2 2\pi i/n}$ and the reduction of sums modulo prime powers $p^\alpha$.
result.transcription:
$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\cos(x^2+\delta)\,\partial x=\Delta$
[-$\Delta=\Sigma\int_0^\beta\cos(x+\pi/\beta)^2\partial x$-]
$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\cos(\alpha x^2+\delta)\partial x=\frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{\alpha}}=\sum_{-\infty,\infty}\int_0^\beta\cos(\alpha x^2+2\alpha\beta[?]x+\alpha\beta^2+\delta)\partial x$
$\pi f x=\sum_{\infty,-\infty}\cos nx\int_0^\pi f t\cos nt\,\partial t$
$\pi\left(f x+f(2\pi-x)+f(2\pi+x)\quad\quad+f(h2\pi-x)\right)=\sum_{\infty,-\infty}\cos nx\int_0^{h2\pi}f t\cos nt\,\partial t$
$2\alpha\beta=1\quad\alpha\beta^2=2m\pi\quad\beta=4m\pi\quad\alpha=\frac{1}{8m\pi}$
$\pi.2\sum_0^{h-1}\cos\left(\frac{s^2 4\pi^2}{8m\pi}+\delta\right)=\Delta\sqrt{8m\pi}$
$\pi\sum_{0,n-1}\cos\left(\frac{s^2 2\pi}{n}+\delta\right)=\Delta\sqrt{2n\pi}\quad n\equiv 0\,(\mathrm{mod}\,4)$
$\pi\,2(\cos\delta-\sin\delta)=2\Delta\sqrt{2\pi}$
$\sum_{0,n-1}\cos\left(\frac{s^2 2\pi}{n}+\delta\right)=(\cos\delta-\sin\delta)\sqrt{n}\quad n\equiv 0\bmod 4$
